children: Stocks and crypto head into a holiday-shortened week still reeling from one of their worst stretches in years. The Nasdaq 100 lost more than 10% last week, its steepest weekly fall since the Covid crash of 2020. Bitcoin dropped to its lowest level in over two years before bouncing back toward $61,000. Fresh inflation and growth data, plus billions of dollars in possible forced selling, now threaten another round of losses.
Nvidia and Anthropic Lead a Brutal Week for Tech

Nvidia plunged 23% last week, its sharpest weekly drop in 18 years. That extended a seven-week losing streak, the chipmaker’s longest since the 2008 financial crisis. The slide comes amid turmoil at Nvidia following Jensen Huang’s exit.
Anthropic had a wild debut:
The Claude maker raised a record $93.5 billion in its IPO, plus another $26 billion from tech giants that bought at the offer price.
Shares jumped 17% on Thursday, lifting its market value to $1.8 trillion.
The rally faded fast. The stock fell 8.5% on Friday to close at $88.91 and slipped another 1.25% to $87.80 in after-hours trade.
Its fully diluted market value of $1.6 trillion still ranks behind only six US companies.
Events That Could Move Markets This Week
Monday, November 23:
S&P Global services and manufacturing PMI data for November
Tuesday, November 24:
November consumer confidence
Wednesday, November 25:
October PCE inflation, the second reading of Q3 GDP and October new home sales
Thursday, November 26:
US markets closed for Thanksgiving
Friday, November 27:
early close for US stock markets

Wednesday is the big day. Headline PCE inflation is expected to rise to 3.8% from 3.6%, close to double the Fed’s 2% target. Markets already price in a 90% chance of a 25 basis point rate hike in December, and a hotter reading could raise fears of even tighter policy. The first estimate put Q3 GDP growth at 3.4%. A downward revision while inflation keeps rising would add to worries that the economy is slowing and prices aren’t cooling.
Bitcoin Bounces From a Two-Year Low

Bitcoin fell to nearly $55,000, its lowest since September 2024, before rebounding. The bounce came from the $53,000 to $56,000 zone, where the price found support several times between July and September 2024.
The 3-day RSI has fallen deep into oversold territory. Past oversold readings were followed by relief rallies of very different lengths:
Early June 2026:
a bounce of about a week, then a lower low
Early February 2026:
a relief rally that lasted until about mid-May
Mid to late November 2025:
a local low that held until mid-January
The weekly Supertrend is still red, so a short relief rally looks more likely than a full trend reversal. Bitcoin is already struggling at $61,000.
Ethereum and XRP Test Key Support

Ethereum is bouncing from its $1,510 to $1,570 support zone, and its latest low formed right in the middle of that range. A short-term recovery could test $1,730 to $1,820. Choppy sideways trading is likely, though, and a lower low later remains possible.

XRP is showing an early bullish divergence on the daily chart, with lower lows in price and higher lows in the RSI. The signal still needs one to two more days to confirm. A close at or above $0.93 would keep XRP’s last major weekly support intact.
What’s Next: Key Levels to Watch
Bitcoin:
Resistance at $61,000 to $62,000, then $65,000 to $67,000. Support at $53,000 to $56,000, with heavy liquidity near $52,000.
Ethereum:
Resistance at $1,730 to $1,820. Support at $1,510 to $1,570.
XRP:
Resistance at $0.99 to $1.02. Weekly support near $0.93.
Stocks:
Wednesday’s PCE and GDP data, and how much systematic funds sell into thin holiday trading.

title: Nvidia, Anthropic, XRP and Bitcoin Brace for a Volatile Thanksgiving Week
